# Eurostat Indicators Explorer

**[Open the live app](https://sedzinfo.shinyapps.io/golemeurostat/)** ·
[Website](https://sedzinfo.github.io/golemeurostat/)

A Shiny app, built as a golem package, for exploring indicators of
[Eurostat](https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat), the statistical office of the
European Union: for the 27 countries of the EU, the 4 of EFTA and the 9
candidate countries, with the EU-27 average for comparison, and for the
regions of Europe. It follows the design of
[golemworldbank](https://github.com/sedzinfo/golemworldbank), and shares
its stylesheets and scripts, which both apps load from
[sedzinfo.github.io](https://github.com/sedzinfo/sedzinfo.github.io/tree/main/shiny):
the layout of the page, on a desktop and on a phone, and the dark mode.

## Tabs

The same tabs as golemworldbank, plus a second map for the regions of
Europe:

- **Country Comparison**: an indicator over the years for the countries
  you pick, with the EU-27 average as a dashed line
- **Indicator Comparison**: several indicators over the years for one
  country, or the EU-27
- **Pyramid**: the population of a country by five-year age group and
  sex, animated by year
- **Barplot**: the countries ranked by an indicator, as a race through
  the years, with the country you pick in red
- **Scatterplot**: the countries by two indicators, as bubbles as large
  as their population, animated by year, with the correlation of the two
  in each year
- **Map**: the countries colored by an indicator, from red for the
  lowest through white to dark blue for the highest, animated by year
- **Regions**: the regions of Europe (NUTS 2) colored in the same way by
  an indicator, such as GDP per inhabitant or unemployment, animated by
  year
- **Change (%)**: the indicators of a country that rose and fell between
  two years, by how much: by percent, and those that are percentages,
  such as the unemployment rate, by percentage points, in tabs of their
  own
- **Indicators**: every indicator of the app, with its unit, definition
  and a link to its dataset at Eurostat
- **About**: where the data comes from, the acknowledgments and the
  license

The lists of countries of Country Comparison, Indicator Comparison and
Barplot offer only the countries that have values of the indicator, or
indicators, picked, as most indicators have none for Ukraine, Georgia,
Moldova or Liechtenstein. A country picked that has none is set aside,
and comes back with the next indicator that has values for it.

The indicators are the 62 chosen by hand and, after them, the series of
Eurostat’s main tables, about 1,500 more, in the groups of Eurostat’s
themes. Type in a list of indicators to search their names, or the code
of a dataset, such as `une_rt_a`.

## Installation

### Prerequisites

1.  **Install R**: <https://cran.r-project.org/>
2.  **Install RStudio** (optional but recommended):
    <https://posit.co/downloads/>

### Package Installation

Open RStudio (or an R console) and run:

[`install.packages`](https://rdrr.io/r/utils/install.packages.html)`(`` `` ``"golemeurostat"``,`` `` repos ``=`` `[`c`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/c.html)`(``"https://sedzinfo.r-universe.dev"``, ``"https://cloud.r-project.org"``)`` ``)`

[R-universe](https://sedzinfo.r-universe.dev/golemeurostat) builds
golemeurostat from this repository, and CRAN provides the packages it
needs.

To install from GitHub instead:

`# Install devtools if you haven't already`` `[`install.packages`](https://rdrr.io/r/utils/install.packages.html)`(``"devtools"``)`` ``# Install golemeurostat from GitHub`` ``devtools``::`[`install_github`](https://devtools.r-lib.org/reference/install-deprecated.html)`(``"sedzinfo/golemeurostat"``)`

Or install the source tarball of the [latest
release](https://github.com/sedzinfo/golemeurostat/releases/tag/latest),
which is rebuilt from `main` on every change, together with the PDF
manual:

[`install.packages`](https://rdrr.io/r/utils/install.packages.html)`(`` `` ``"https://github.com/sedzinfo/golemeurostat/releases/download/latest/golemeurostat_0.0.0.9000.tar.gz"``,`` `` repos ``=`` ``NULL``, type ``=`` ``"source"`` ``)`

## Usage

From the package folder:

`pkgload``::`[`load_all`](https://pkgload.r-lib.org/reference/load_all.html)`(``)`` `[`run_app`](https://sedzinfo.github.io/golemeurostat/reference/run_app.md)`(``)`

`app.R`, which the deployment runs, starts it with
`run_app(analytics = TRUE)`: Google Analytics, through the cookie banner
shared with the sites of sedzinfo.github.io, which loads it only after
the visitor accepts, and a footer with the Cookie settings and Privacy
links, as in golemworldbank. Without it, the app sends nothing.

The data and the charts can also be used from R:

[`indicators`](https://sedzinfo.github.io/golemeurostat/reference/indicators.md)`(``)`` ``# the catalogue of indicators`` ``unemployment`` ``<-`` `[`get_indicator`](https://sedzinfo.github.io/golemeurostat/reference/get_indicator.md)`(``"unemployment"``)`` `[`plot_country_comp`](https://sedzinfo.github.io/golemeurostat/reference/plot_country_comp.md)`(``unemployment``, `[`c`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/c.html)`(``"EL"``, ``"BG"``, ``"PT"``)``, ``"unemployment"``)`` `[`plot_regions`](https://sedzinfo.github.io/golemeurostat/reference/plot_regions.md)`(`[`get_regional`](https://sedzinfo.github.io/golemeurostat/reference/get_regional.md)`(``"r_gdp_pps"``)``, ``"r_gdp_pps"``)`

Eurostat codes the countries with two letters, as ISO does, except
Greece, which is `EL`.

## Adding an indicator

The indicators come from two files of `inst/extdata`, with the same
columns: `indicators.csv`, written by hand, and
`indicators_generated.csv`, written by a script from the catalogue of
Eurostat.

### By hand

An indicator added to `indicators.csv` comes first in the lists, under
its own topic, and needs no R code:

| Column | Contents |
|----|----|
| `id` | A short name, lower case letters, digits and `_` |
| `level` | `country`, or `region` for the Regions tab |
| `topic`, `name`, `unit` | How the app shows it |
| `dataset` | The code of the Eurostat dataset, such as `une_rt_a` |
| `filters` | The value of each of the other dimensions of the dataset, such as `sex=T;age=Y15-74;unit=PC_ACT`, so that one value is left per country and year |
| `definition` | A sentence for the Indicators tab |

The code of a dataset and of its dimensions are in the [Eurostat data
browser](https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/databrowser/).
`check_indicators("your_id")` tries a new row: it reports the countries
or regions and the years it has, or what is wrong with it, such as a
dimension that Eurostat does not know or one left open, which gives more
than one value per country and year. Run
[`check_indicators()`](https://sedzinfo.github.io/golemeurostat/reference/check_indicators.md)
now and then to check them all, as Eurostat sometimes renames or retires
a dataset.

### From Eurostat’s main tables

`indicators_generated.csv` holds the series of the [main
tables](https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/web/main/data/database) of
Eurostat, its own selection of headline indicators with few breakdowns
(codes such as `tps00001`, `tec00115` or `sdg_08_10`). To rebuild it, as
Eurostat adds, renames and retires tables, run from the package folder:

[`source`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/source.html)`(``"data-raw/build_indicators.R"``)`

The script reads Eurostat’s table of contents and the dimensions of
every dataset, downloads each main table with yearly data once (about
680 tables, about 10 minutes the first time; the downloads are kept a
week in `data-raw/cache`), and writes a row for each series, a
combination of the dimensions other than the country and the year, that
has values for at least 10 countries, or 50 regions for the Regions tab,
up to 2015 or later. A table with more than 10 such series is left out,
and so are amounts in national currency, which cannot be compared
between countries, and a series that another table already has under the
same name. The names come from the titles of the tables and the labels
of the codes, and the units from the labels of the units; the topic is
the folder of the table in Eurostat’s themes. These limits are at the
top of the script. Some labels of Eurostat do not describe their series,
such as a unit of “Percentage” for amounts or a title in tonnes for
values in kilograms, and some tables have no unit at all:
`data-raw/corrections.csv` gives the unit, and the name or definition
when they are wrong too, for the series of a table or those with a code,
such as `unit=RT`, with the reason, and the script says when a
correction no longer finds its series. At its end, it runs
`data-raw/build_values.R`, which writes `inst/extdata/values.rds`, the
values of every indicator of the countries (about 750,000, 1 MB), for
the Change (%) tab, `regions.rds` and `pyramids.rds`, the values of
every indicator of the regions and the population of each country by age
group and sex (0.5 MB together), and
`inst/app/www/countries_RG_20M_2024_4326.geojson`, the outlines of the
countries of the Map tab.

A generated row that downloads the same as a hand-written one is left
out, so to rename or describe a generated indicator better, copy its row
to `indicators.csv` and change it there.

## Data

Each indicator is downloaded from the Eurostat API, which needs no key,
the first time a tab shows it, and kept on disk for a day, in
`tools::R_user_dir("golemeurostat", "cache")`; set
`options(golemeurostat.cache_dir = )` to keep it elsewhere. A few values
that are plainly wrong in Eurostat’s data, such as a share of the
population of 933.2% in a year between two of about 94%, are listed in
`inst/extdata/errors.csv`, with the reason, and left out for as long as
Eurostat gives them; a value more than 1,000 times the median of its
year and of its country, in the wrong units, is left out too. The
outlines of the countries and regions of the maps, the NUTS 2024
classification, come from
[GISCO](https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/web/gisco): those of the regions
are downloaded once, and those of the countries are in the package, with
Moldova and Georgia, which the classification leaves out, from GISCO’s
outlines of the countries. The Change (%) tab, which compares all the
indicators of a country at once, uses instead the values written into
the package by `data-raw/build_values.R`, and says their date. The same
saved values work without internet:
[`saved_indicator()`](https://sedzinfo.github.io/golemeurostat/reference/saved_indicator.md),
[`saved_regional()`](https://sedzinfo.github.io/golemeurostat/reference/saved_regional.md)
and
[`saved_pyramid()`](https://sedzinfo.github.io/golemeurostat/reference/saved_pyramid.md)
give them in the shape of
[`get_indicator()`](https://sedzinfo.github.io/golemeurostat/reference/get_indicator.md),
[`get_regional()`](https://sedzinfo.github.io/golemeurostat/reference/get_regional.md)
and
[`get_pyramid()`](https://sedzinfo.github.io/golemeurostat/reference/get_pyramid.md),
and the examples of the charts use them, such as
`plot_bar(saved_indicator("unemployment"), "unemployment", country = "EL", top_n = 10)`.

Source of the data: Eurostat. Administrative boundaries: ©
EuroGeographics.

## Development

Run the tests with
[`devtools::test()`](https://devtools.r-lib.org/reference/test.html),
which use saved Eurostat answers and need no internet, and the full
package check with
[`devtools::check()`](https://devtools.r-lib.org/reference/check.html).

# Package index

## App

- [`run_app()`](https://sedzinfo.github.io/golemeurostat/reference/run_app.md)
  : Run the Eurostat Indicators Explorer

## Data

The catalogue of indicators and countries, downloading an indicator from
Eurostat for the countries or the regions, or the population of a
country by age and sex, checking the catalogue against Eurostat, and the
values of all the indicators that the Change (%) tab compares; the
values of an indicator of the countries or the regions, or the
population of a country by age and sex, as saved in the package, without
internet, which the examples of the charts use

- [`all_values()`](https://sedzinfo.github.io/golemeurostat/reference/all_values.md)
  : The values of all the indicators
- [`check_indicators()`](https://sedzinfo.github.io/golemeurostat/reference/check_indicators.md)
  : Check the catalogue against Eurostat
- [`countries()`](https://sedzinfo.github.io/golemeurostat/reference/countries.md)
  : The countries of the app
- [`get_indicator()`](https://sedzinfo.github.io/golemeurostat/reference/get_indicator.md)
  : Get an indicator for the countries
- [`get_pyramid()`](https://sedzinfo.github.io/golemeurostat/reference/get_pyramid.md)
  : Get the population of a country by age group and sex
- [`get_regional()`](https://sedzinfo.github.io/golemeurostat/reference/get_regional.md)
  : Get an indicator for the regions
- [`indicator_change()`](https://sedzinfo.github.io/golemeurostat/reference/indicator_change.md)
  : Indicators that rose or fell between two years for one country
- [`indicators()`](https://sedzinfo.github.io/golemeurostat/reference/indicators.md)
  : The indicators of the app
- [`saved_indicator()`](https://sedzinfo.github.io/golemeurostat/reference/saved_indicator.md)
  : Get an indicator for the countries, as saved in the package
- [`saved_pyramid()`](https://sedzinfo.github.io/golemeurostat/reference/saved_pyramid.md)
  : Get the population of a country by age group and sex, as saved in
  the package
- [`saved_regional()`](https://sedzinfo.github.io/golemeurostat/reference/saved_regional.md)
  : Get an indicator for the regions, as saved in the package

## Plot

The plotly charts of the tabs: country and indicator comparisons,
population pyramid, ranked bars, maps of the countries and of the
regions, scatter plot

- [`plot_bar()`](https://sedzinfo.github.io/golemeurostat/reference/plot_bar.md)
  : Ranked bars of an indicator, animated by year
- [`plot_country_comp()`](https://sedzinfo.github.io/golemeurostat/reference/plot_country_comp.md)
  : Line chart of an indicator for several countries
- [`plot_indicator_comp()`](https://sedzinfo.github.io/golemeurostat/reference/plot_indicator_comp.md)
  : Line chart of several indicators for one country
- [`plot_map()`](https://sedzinfo.github.io/golemeurostat/reference/plot_map.md)
  : Map of the countries, animated by year
- [`plot_pyramid()`](https://sedzinfo.github.io/golemeurostat/reference/plot_pyramid.md)
  : Population pyramid, animated by year
- [`plot_regions()`](https://sedzinfo.github.io/golemeurostat/reference/plot_regions.md)
  : Map of the regions, animated by year
- [`plot_scatter()`](https://sedzinfo.github.io/golemeurostat/reference/plot_scatter.md)
  : Scatter plot of two indicators, animated by year

The tables of the Change (%) and Indicators tabs

  as a DataTable

- [`render_index_table()`](https://sedzinfo.github.io/golemeurostat/reference/render_index_table.md)
  : Table of the indicators
